description:
*This is a Pre-Book, Bikes Will Deliver in June 2027*
Then it will return to full price.

It’s the ultimate lightweight geared cyclocross race bike. Most likely the last true CX racer that we'll ever put into production as CX has become fairly niche.

It’ll go anywhere, but the features, or lack thereof, speak to its intended purpose. Two bottle mounts. No fenders, no racks. Simple and extremely light. In addition to its CX chops, you’ll find it to be a wonderful tool for all-road, singletrack, and gravel.

Designers Notes
Pure CX performance. As we no longer need our cyclocross bikes to also be all-arounders, the Tiger Mask has aggressive race geometry: a tallish (66mm) bb height and a short 420mm rear end. It fits a 45c tire in the back and is a riot in the dirt. It’s way more flickable on trail than a modern gravel bike, which prioritize stability over agility. Strangely enough, for some riders, the short wheelbase and lively handling will actually make it the “gravel” bike they’ve been dreaming of. I also highly recommend it for all-road use as the geo difference between an All-Road bike and a cross bike largely boils down to about 4mm of bottom bracket drop.

Note on Name - This bike is the final boss in a lineage of cross bikes that I've been involved in that includes Nature Boy, Macho Man, Macho King, the Mean Jean, etc. I have a history of doing wrestling themed names and decided to continue the tradition here. Tiger Mask was a Japanese Manga character from the 1960's, a villainous heel who turned to good after realizing the negative example he was setting for the nation's youth. In the 1980's New Japan Pro Wrestling licensed the character and brought it to life. Since then five different athletes have portrayed the heroic character.
- Jeff
